findings.condition: The acceptance band requires tau in [0.9525 ms, 1.0335 ms]. Nominal R1*C1 = 1.000 ms gives 0.63212 V (passes), but neither R1 nor C1 carries a tolerance specification, and any combined RC deviation beyond -4.75%/+3.35% violates the band (symmetric +/-3.4% is the first failure; +/-5% and +/-10% fail on both edges).

evidence.locator: symbol R1 property Value '10k'; symbol C1 property Value '100n' (no tolerance fields)

findings.mechanism: V(1 ms) = 1 - exp(-1 ms/tau); the band maps directly to a tau window. Common E-series parts are sold at tolerances (resistors +/-1%, ceramic capacitors frequently +/-5% to +/-10%, plus class-2 dielectric voltage/temperature coefficients) that can exceed the available window, so a physically built board can fail the only stated requirement while the design files pass every native check.
findings.reasoning: Labeled a concern, not a defect: nominal values satisfy the criterion and the packet forbids imposing unstated ratings, so I cannot assert which tolerance grade would be fitted. But the criterion is a voltage band, and compliance of manufactured units is unestablished because the design specifies no tolerance; the margin arithmetic (-4.75%/+3.35% combined) is established by calculation. Severity major because this is the sole stated acceptance criterion and plausible standard parts exceed the window.
findings.title: 0.62-0.65 V @ 1 ms band leaves only -4.75%/+3.35% combined RC margin and no tolerances are specified

findings.condition: All four supplied checks are structural (ERC, DRC with parity, netlist export, geometry probe). None applies a stimulus or measures /OUT, so their clean exits provide zero evidence for the 0.62-0.65 V @ 1 ms requirement the scope asks about.
findings.mechanism: A successful tool exit proves rule compliance, not electrical behavior. The settling criterion depends on R and C values and loading, which ERC/DRC do not evaluate; the only quantitative evidence is the transient simulation performed in this review (0.63212 V at 1 ms, unloaded).
findings.reasoning: This is a verification-coverage finding, not a design defect: the design's nominal behavior does meet the band once actually simulated. It is reportable because the packet's evidence set, taken alone, could not support either a pass or fail verdict on the stated scope question.
findings.title: Packet checks never exercise the settling criterion; nominal electrical behavior verified only by this review

findings.condition: The requirement is stated for /OUT connected to a switched ADC input, but sampling capacitance, switch resistance, initial charge and timing are explicitly unspecified. No check or artifact evaluates any loading case.

evidence.locator: ADC charge-share bound 1.95 nF; DC-load bound 16.3 kOhm
'ADC sampling capacitance, switch resistance, initial charge and sampling timing have not been specified'

findings.location: inputs/requirements.txt (scope: 'while connected to a switched ADC input'); J1 pad 2 (/OUT) in inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb
findings.mechanism: Bounding analysis (no ADC behavior invented): instantaneous charge sharing with a zero-charged sampling capacitor Cs droops the output by V*Cs/(C+Cs); Cs must exceed ~1.95 nF to pull 0.632 V below the 0.620 V lower limit at the sampling instant. A continuous resistive load below ~16.3 kOhm drops even the asymptotic value below 0.62 V. Within these bounds the design is robust; outside them it is not, and the packet provides no basis to choose.
findings.reasoning: Missing coverage rather than a defect, per the scope's own instruction to separate the two. The computed bounds show typical SAR-class sampling capacitances (picofarad range) would be negligible, but asserting that would invent ADC behavior; what is established is only the boundary at which the criterion would fail, and that no supplied evidence covers any loaded case.
findings.title: Criterion verified only with /OUT unloaded; switched-ADC interaction unbounded by the packet but bounded here

findings.condition: There is no F.Cu path between C1 pad 2 and J1 pad 3; the only GND return is F.Cu track -> one 0.3 mm-drill via -> B.Cu zone -> four thermal spokes into J1.3. Independent probe of the saved fill confirms the path is continuous: fill contains the via center and covers 12/24 sampled points on the J1.3 annulus.

evidence.locator: via at (113,100) drill 0.3 net GND; GND track C1.2->(113,100)
zone (net GND) (layer B.Cu) connect_pads clearance 0.5, thermal_bridge_width 0.5

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb: via uuid b71a70d7 at (113,100); B.Cu zone uuid 38a83012; J1 pad 3 at (100,105.08)
findings.mechanism: A single via and thermal-relief spokes form the sole return conductor. For this signal-level RC (microamp-scale transient currents, ~26 mOhm of 0.25 mm trace against a 10 kOhm source impedance) the electrical effect on the criterion is negligible; the observation is a robustness/manufacturing note (one drill defect or spoke void opens the GND net), not a performance issue.
findings.reasoning: Reported as informational: connectivity is positively verified on the saved fill and no stated requirement (current, redundancy, qualification) is violated. Included because the single-point return is the one physically fragile element of an otherwise trivially robust board, and because the fill-as-saved caveat in the packet's own DRC/geometry limitations makes this path the item most worth re-checking after any board edit.
findings.title: GND continuity between C1 and connector relies on a single 0.6/0.3 mm via plus zone thermal spokes (verified connected as saved)

limitations: ADC sampling capacitance, switch resistance, initial charge and sampling timing are unspecified by the packet; the settling criterion was verified only for an unloaded /OUT plus bounding analysis. No ADC model was assumed.

Component tolerances are not specified in the design (R1 '10k', C1 '100n' with no tolerance fields); the criterion was verified at nominal values only. No specific part model or dielectric was assumed.

Copper thickness/stackup is not specified in the board file; series trace/via parasitics were assessed only qualitatively (tens of mOhm against a 10 kOhm source impedance, negligible to the criterion). No ampacity or thermal qualification was performed or inferred — no current requirement is stated.
Zone fill was evaluated exactly as saved; the read-only candidate forbids a refill pass, so fill correctness after any future edit is not covered.

Source step fidelity (1 V ideal step at J1.1) was assumed per the stated exercise; source impedance of the external driver is unspecified and adds directly to R1 (e.g. 50 ohm adds +0.5% to tau), which was not budgeted anywhere.
No thermal, vibration, or connector mating analysis performed (artificial toolchain fixture per inputs/requirements.txt; no such requirements stated).
